Former Synagogue in Rülzheim

Former Synagogue · Rülzheim, Germany

The synagogue in Rülzheim, one of the largest rural Jewish communities in the southern Palatinate, was built in 1832–33 to designs by architect August von Voit, replacing an earlier prayer house on the same site in the Kuntzengasse. During the November 1938 pogrom its interior, roof, and windows were destroyed, but the structure itself survived. After the war it served various secular uses, including as storage and later a youth center, before the municipality acquired and restored it. Placed under monument protection in 1986, it reopened in 1991 as a history and community center, now part of Rülzheim's 'Centrum für Kunst und Kultur.'
